test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: An express train travelled at an average speed of 100 km/h, stopping for 3 min after every 75 km. How much time it took the express train to travel 600 km?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Running Time** = (600 ÷ 100) × 60 = 360 min.

**Number of Stoppages** = (600 ÷ 75) − 1 = 8 − 1 = 7 (excluding the destination).

**Total Stoppage Time** = 7 × 3 = 21 min.

**Total Time** = 360 + 21 = 381 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 381 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average speed = 100 km/h, Distance = 600 km, Stoppage interval = 75 km, Stoppage duration = 3 min.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed; Total Time = Running Time + Stoppage Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c70cadd5ca867e1702d3ab3ee873ffa919a61d5e69cfa1d492ab1b264e7f557a.png] 

⇒ **Running Time** = 600 ÷ 100 = 6 hours

⇒ **Running Time in minutes** = 6 × 60 = 360 min

⇒ **Number of intervals** = 600 ÷ 75 = 8

⇒ Since the last stop is the **destination**, we subtract 1: 8 − 1 = 7 stoppages

⇒ **Total Stoppage Time** = 7 × 3 = 21 min

⇒ **Total Time** = 360 + 21 = 381 min

**∴ The correct answer is 381 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Speed with Stoppages

When a vehicle stops, its effective speed decreases. Effective speed = Total Distance ÷ (Running time + Stoppage time).

Stoppage Logic

In problems where a journey ends exactly at a multiple of the stoppage interval, the last stop is ignored because it is the destination. Use (Total Distance ÷ Interval) − 1.

Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. In this case, 600 km ÷ (381/60) h ≈ 94.48 km/h.</p
